messages:
Devon Park: Quick FYI — Yesterday at ~22:13 UTC quota-enforcer reported a bunch of org-level bursts hitting SLO, but billing sees higher billed tokens for a few orgs. Looks like retries + tool calls might be double-counting. Anyone seen this pattern? /cc @Maria

Maria Chen: Saw that too. A few customers pinged support with sudden token spikes + concurrent 429s. On the console per-key limiter showed token budget depleted, but the request traces show multiple retries with the same X-Request-ID.

Alex Rivera: Do we surface client_request_id anywhere in the quota-enforcer logs? We only store internal req_id. If clients set X-Request-ID we don't use it for dedupe right now.

Samir Gupta: Infra logs show repeated lines for the same user token within a ~200ms window, e.g.:

InfraBot: log: REQUEST user=org-92 req_id=abcd1234 client_req=cli-req-9 tokens_prompt=120 tokens_completion=80 tool_calls=1 retry=1 billed=400

Devon Park: Example above — billed=400 but 120+80+(toolcalls?) doesn't match. My hunch: tool calls are counted both as completion tokens and again as separate tool tokens. Retries then re-apply both.

Maria Chen: Hypothesis: Metering pipeline aggregates tool invocation tokens in one stage, then a later completion re-calculation adds completion tokens again after retry because we replay the model output, so duplicates happen. Also caching affects token estimation on retries.

Alex Rivera: Repro plan: send a request that triggers 2 tool calls returning small snippets, then force a retry by dropping the response (simulate network blip) while preserving X-Request-ID. If billed delta > expected, we've reproduced. I can draft a script.

Anya Li: Short-term mitigation suggestions:
- Stop counting toolcall tokens as an independent billing axis until we confirm (flip to non-billing mode behind feature flag).
- Add a dedupe window in quota-enforcer keyed by X-Request-ID (5s) to avoid double-deducting burst credits on fast retries.
- Expose a per-org "dedupe_hits" metric so we can monitor impact in the console.

Samir Gupta: I'll add an emergency metric + alert to eng-sre: fire if dedupe_hits / requests > 0.5% in prod for any org. Also will push a small change to quota-enforcer to check client-provided ID before applying burst deductions.

InfraBot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled to edgeloop pool (us-west2) at 03:30 UTC. Auto-rollback if error rate delta > 0.1% over 5m.

Devon Park: We also need a billing audit to surface retro adjustments if we overcharged. @Maria can you own the billing diff investigation? ETA EOD?

Maria Chen: On it. Will pull the billing exports, compare per-org token tallies against metering logs, and create a repro repo. I'll add QA steps. Link to repro (internal): https://git.internal/redwood/repros/quota-dedupe

Alex Rivera: I'll prepare a small PR that: (1) uses X-Request-ID dedupe in quota-enforcer logic, (2) gates toolcall separate-counting behind a kill-switch flag, and (3) adds unit tests for retry accounting. Also will update the docs with clear wording about how tool calls vs completion tokens are billed.

Devon Park: Action items recap: Samir add metric + alert and patch quota-enforcer, Alex open PR + docs + tests, Maria audit billing + create repro, Anya own console metric/visualization. We'll sync tomorrow for rollout strategy. :thumbsup:

Anya Li: One more UX note — console should show a small "dedupe adjusted" badge on the org billing timeline when we apply adjustments so customers aren't confused. I'll sketch a mock and post in #product tomorrow.

Samir Gupta: I'll post the initial canary results in this thread after the deploy.

Devon Park: Thanks everyone. If we confirm a customer-facing billing impact we'll coordinate comms with ops and support.

Maria Chen: +1. Filing follow-ups now.
